Gateshead Gross Value Added, 2024

Gross value added (GVA) is the value of everything produced in the borough, less what was used up producing it. This dashboard covers Gateshead's GVA from 1998 to 2024 in cash and real terms, by industry, against the North East, England and the UK, the seven NEMSA authorities and Gateshead's ONS economic statistical neighbours. It is built on the ONS balanced GVA release of , which adds 2024 and revises every earlier year.

Key Findings

Output and Real Growth

Current prices are the cash value of output in each year and include inflation. Chained volume measures remove price changes, so they are the right measure of real growth over time. Growth rates on this tab are our calculations from the published ONS levels.

    About This Dashboard

    Suppressed Areas

    Productivity

    GVA per hour worked and per filled job for 2024 are due from ONS on 5 November 2026, in the subregional productivity release. Until then the 2023 figures stay in the Gateshead Productivity & GVA dashboard, which runs on the previous GVA edition. This dashboard does not mix the two editions.

    Measures

    • GVA at current basic prices is the cash value of output in each year, in pounds million. It includes inflation, so it is best for comparing areas in a single year
    • GVA in chained volume measures removes price changes, expressed in money. It is the measure for real growth over time. Chained volumes are not additive, so industries do not sum to the total
    • GDP per head at current market prices is ONS's published gross domestic product divided by resident population. GDP adds taxes less subsidies on products to GVA. Because GVA is counted where people work and population where they live, per head figures are pushed up in places with many in-commuters and down in places with many out-commuters
    • GVA per employee job divides current price GVA by BRES employee jobs for the same year. BRES excludes most self-employment, so levels are an approximation and are best read as a comparison between industries. Real estate is left out because its GVA includes owner-occupiers' imputed rent, which has no jobs attached

      Notes and Caveats

      • The latest year is provisional and will be revised in the next edition
      • Every earlier year has been revised in this edition, partly because of new deflation methods and the move to ITL25 geography, so figures here should not be mixed with the previous edition
      • North East, England and UK figures are the published ONS region and country totals. UK totals and growth include Extra-Regio (mainly offshore oil and gas), as in the ONS headline. UK industry shares use the UK less Extra-Regio, so they are on the same basis as the regions
      • Local authority GVA can be volatile from year to year, especially for small areas and single industries. ONS advises caution with erratic movements
      • ONS allocates GVA for public administration and health to local authorities using BRES employment, and education partly so. Local real terms movements in these industries follow employment and national price measures closely, so they say little about local performance
      • GVA is administrative and modelled data with no published confidence intervals, so no error bars are drawn
      • Business counts are UK Business Counts enterprises. Size bands are rounded for disclosure and sum to slightly less than the published total, so band shares use the band sum

      Assurance

      GVA, GDP per head, employment and business count levels are official published figures quoted directly. Growth rates, ranks, shares, revisions and GVA per employee job are our calculations from those figures. The build reconciles the twelve North East local authorities to the published North East total in every year. This is an analytical product, not official statistics, assured to the Aqua Book's dashboard tier. The assumptions log and known limitations are in the repository's analytical assurance note.

      Next Refresh

      ONS expects to publish the complete dataset, with the suppressed areas restored, within four to six weeks of . When it lands the dashboard is rebuilt from the new files with no design changes, because every chart and sentence reads from the data.
